name: create-external-interface-and-type-stubs
description: Contract `7.5.0`'s two stub kinds authored with no new tool and no new address form. One `create` declares an interface another file of the same delivery owns — its full AUTOSAR path and its `DEST`, nothing of its content — a second declares an implementation data type the same way, and one `update` re-points a component's port at the interface stub. A stub is an ordinary element to the editing protocol: the generic change set reaches both because the registry is derived from the contract.

context.summary: The `examples/basic` model, whose `ExampleConsumerSWC` requires `IExample` on `rIn` through the connector `Example_to_Consumer`. Neither stub the change set creates exists.

authorization.notes: Three exact addresses in two layers and the component's port. No component, element or port here carries a level, so the safety guard has nothing to ask: re-pointing a RATED consumer's port from a source carrying a rated data element to a stub is the one move through a stub that asks, and it is `packages/tools/tests/test_external_stubs_editing.py`'s to pin.

input.intent: Carry the speed interface and its type as references into the rest of the delivery.

value.name: IForeignSpeed
value.description: Declared by another file of the same delivery

after.name: IForeignSpeed
after.description: Declared by another file of the same delivery

expected.notes: A stub has five fields and no member at all: `name`, the `kind` discriminator, `external_ref`, `external_dest` and `description`. `external_ref` and `external_dest` are what the generated ARXML carries verbatim on every reference naming the stub, and no element is emitted for the stub itself. Whether the pair is well formed — an absolute path, a `DEST` the role admits — is `interface.external-incomplete-reference` and `data-type.external-incomplete-reference`, both pass D's; `negative/consistency-violation-interface-external-incomplete-reference.json` and its data type twin are the refusals. The connector stays legal because the kind is compared across a stub: a `SENDER-RECEIVER-INTERFACE` stub is sender-receiver, and nothing beyond the kind is judged, since the model cannot see what the target declares.
